author: WhyOS-Apps contributors
description:
The badge as a USB keyboard and mouse for a computer. Save texts you
type often, such as an address, a long command or a login sequence,
and let the badge type them.

Typing a text:
- Connect the computer to the badge's bottom USB-C port, and unplug the
  side port: while it is connected, the computer does not see the badge.
- Click where the text should go, choose the text in the list and press
  Enter. Esc stops the typing.

Making a text: the triangle adds one, the cross edits it, and the
square has the other options (type, edit, move, delete). A text has a
name for the list and up to 1000 bytes. In the editor:
- Shift+Enter starts a new line, Tab types a tab.
- Shift with Esc, Backspace or an arrow puts in that key.
- Ctrl or Alt with a key puts in that shortcut, such as Ctrl+C.
- The square puts in any other key or shortcut, such as F5, Win+R or
  Ctrl+Alt+Delete.
- The triangle puts in a pause of half a second, for example to let a
  window open after Win+R. Press it again for a longer pause.

Keyboard layout: the badge sends keys, not letters, so set the
computer's layout in the settings (cloud key): US, US International or
US on a Mac. With other layouts, such as German or French, some
characters come out wrong. Accented letters and the euro sign work with
the last two, but you can only add them by editing snippets.txt over
SSH.

Mouse: open the first row of the list. The arrows move the pointer
(tap for one pixel, hold to go faster), Enter is the left button (hold
it to drag), the cross is a right click and Fn+Up/Down scrolls. Keep
awake (the triangle) nudges the pointer every 30 seconds while the app
is open, so the computer does not lock or show you as away. The mouse
needs WhyOS from 2026-10-20 or later.

The texts are stored as plain text on the badge, so do not save
passwords in them.

launch.info: type saved texts, move the mouse

name: HIDeous
summary: HIDeous lets you control your computer using pre-recorded input from your badge.

versions.changelog: The new WhyOS look: the frontpanel's figures behind the screens, calm flat rows and bars, frosted pop-ups with their keys inside. Faster: a key redraws only what changed.
In the editor, the triangle now puts in a pause. The square's list of keys no longer has one. Clearer description.
